messages:
morgan: Heads-up: we had a KV node OOM at 02:11 UTC. Root cause appears to be a steady climb in small-object retention + inter-slab fragmentation after the recent shard-sync change. Posting follow-ups + concrete owners. Keep replies short (claim + ETA).

morgan: Quick action list (priority order):
A) soft eviction threshold and canary rollout (temporary) -> owner: ? -> ETA: 8h
B) three host heap captures + flamegraphs -> owner: ? -> ETA: 24h
C) shard-sync pointer audit (safety) -> owner: ? -> ETA: 48h
D) lightweight fragmentation metric and dashboard -> owner: ? -> ETA: 12h
E) allocator RFC (longer term) -> owner: ? -> ETA: next sprint

hana: I'll take (A) soft eviction. Plan: add `runtime.kv.eviction.soft_limit_pct = 86` to configs, create a canary deploy (10% nodes in us-east-1), watch for increased evictions and latency. ETA 5h.

diego: I'll own (B). Plan: run `rd-heap-capture --pids=kv --secs=90 --out=s3://debug/kv/210445` on nodes alpha/beta/gamma, then run `flameviz` and upload. ETA 18h.

morgan: @hana please make the rollout ops-friendly: include pre/post snapshots for `smem -k` and a Grafana panel link. Also add a flag to emit `kv.soft_eviction` event with shard_id.

hana: noted. adding `kv.soft_eviction` and a short log line `EVT:kv.soft_eviction shard=%s pct=%d` to the runtime.

sara: for (C) pointer audit I can pair with diego after captures are done. we should prioritize review of the commit `shard-sync: reduce copies` (sha: c9a1f2). I want a quick grep for unsafe pointer casts before rolling further. ETA 36h for audit + small fixes.

diego: pairing SGTM. I'll stash the flamegraphs and link them in the ticket.

morgan: (D) metric suggestion: track `runtime.kv.frag_index` computed as (sum(free_frag_bytes)/active_bytes) sampled every 15s per shard; alert if > 0.25 for 10m. Also emit `runtime.kv.small_obj_rate` (count of allocations <256B per minute).

hana: adding both metrics to the agent pipeline. will create a provisional dashboard and a low-priority alert. ETA 10h.

ops-bot: [automated] New ticket created: DEBUG-8819 "KV node OOM - postmortem actions" assigned to unassigned. Link: https://issue.redwood/DEBUG-8819

morgan: very important: do not roll the allocator change wide until we have at least two successful canary cycles. we'll use these signals: `runtime.kv.frag_index`, `srv.oom.count`, `p99.api_lat`. If frag_index drops while p99 stays stable -> good.

diego: question: what rollback criteria for the soft eviction? hana suggested p99 > baseline + 20% or srv.oom.count > 0. agree with that?

sara: yes. also add `errors.eviction_rate` spike > 50% as rollback condition. document exact rollback command: `redwood deploy rollback --service kv-runtime --to previous` and include config reset: `terraform apply -var='kv_eviction_pct=0'`.

hana: made a PR `hana/soft-evict-config` and attached smoke test instructions. link: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/843. Canary deploy in 40m.

diego: capture ids: hc-210445-a (alpha), hc-210445-b (beta). uploading to s3 now.

morgan: good. once uploads complete, diego/sara audit the shard-sync change. if no pointer issues, we proceed to canary compaction changes in a separate patch.

ops-bot: [automated] Ticket DEBUG-8819 updated: tags added {"kv-oom-2026","postmortem-followup"}

sara: long-term: if short mitigations reduce incidents, we'll schedule allocator refactor RFC. estimate 10 dev-weeks; will scope after next retro. also consider small-object pooling to reduce churn.

hana: FYI, I'll add a short-runbook snippet in the ticket: exact commands to force an emergency eviction on a host: `echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/kv/force_evict` and restart sequence.

morgan: last note: set a recurring weekly alert to surface any host with >2 frag_index warnings in 7 days so we catch recurring patterns early. Next sync in 36h. Thanks all.
